# Adoption and Penetration

The growth argument, built from published series rather than from a CAGR someone typed into a slide.

## Observed series

| Series | Start | End | Multiple | CAGR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| NIRF unique institutions | 2,426 (9y span) | 7,692 | 3.17x | 13.7% |
| NIRF total applications | 3,565 (9y span) | 14,163 | 3.97x | 16.6% |
| IICs established | 6,400 (4y span) | 16,367 | 2.56x | 26.5% |
| SRF participating states | 30 (8y span) | 34 | 1.13x | 1.6% |

## What these series mean

- **NIRF unique institutions** - The number of institutions voluntarily entering a ranking regime.
- **NIRF total applications** - Applications across categories - shows multi-category filing.
- **IICs established** - Conflict C-01: the start figure is an earlier official count, the end is the latest.
- **SRF participating states** - State participation is effectively saturated - the only curve that is.

The pattern is important and it is not uniform. Behavioural adoption among institutions is compounding quickly - NIRF participation at 13.7% CAGR, IIC establishment at 26.5% - while *state* participation in SRF is effectively flat at 1.6% because it is saturated at 34 of 34.

The fastest curve is also the one with the smallest base. IIC establishment at 26.5% CAGR is computed on a range whose endpoints come from two different official counts (conflict C-01), so the growth rate is real but the level is contested.

| IIC-bearing (ceiling) | 16,367 | 27.9% |

| NIRF any-category applicants | 7,692 | 13.1% |

## The headroom, and the trap

> Only 1.32% of registered higher education institutions file a NIRF Innovation return, while 24-28% hold an IIC. The gap between those two numbers - roughly 13,000 institutions that are mandated to report and do not - is the structural headroom. It is also the population most likely to be unready, which is why digital readiness (filter 2) and innovation activity (filter 3) remove most of them.

This is the strongest structural argument in the entire research programme, and it is also the most dangerous number in it.

Approximately 13,000 institutions are mandated to report and do not. That gap is either the market or it is the problem, and we currently cannot tell which. If those institutions are unready, then the SAM is 777 and the product has no market - only a compliance chore. That question is F-02 and F-01 in Falsification.md, and it is exactly what the Phase 3B interviews exist to answer.
